subject: Calculating upper and lower lambda for RMSEA

messages.author: 3e12e850fc513291
messages.subject: Calculating upper and lower lambda for RMSEA
parts:
Hi guys!  First of all, sorry for my poor English. It's my second language.

Recently, I've been trying to calculate ECVI's confidence interval in R.

I started with looking up lavaan code for calculating RMSEA's C.I,  because if I figure out how to calculate upper and lower lambda,

all I need to do for the rest is use them to do calculation with other parameters like df and sample size.

However, I'm stuck on the code extracted from "fitmeasures" function, especially for codes in bold.

As far as I know, I would use  qchisq(.05, df, ncp = ncp) and  qchisq(.95,d,ncp=ncp)  to calculate lower and upper lambda respectively.

But clearly, lavaan use another way to do it. Hope someone could help me clarify codes in bold below and why my approach might be wrong.

If there is any related  reference could help me figure it out, please let me know.

I'll really appreciate your help.


 if ("rmsea.ci.lower" %in% fit.measures) {
                lower.lambda <- function(lambda) {
                        (pchisq(X2, df = df, ncp = lambda) - 0.95)
                }
                if (is.na(X2) || is.na(df)) {
                        indices["rmsea.ci.lower"] <- NA
                }
                else if (df < 1 || lower.lambda(0) < 0) {
                        indices["rmsea.ci.lower"] <- 0
                }
                else {
                        lambda.l <- try(uniroot(f = lower.lambda, lower = 0,
                                                upper = X2)$root, silent = TRUE)
                        if (inherits(lambda.l, "try-error")) {
                                lambda.l <- NA
                        }
                        if (object@Options$mimic %in% c("lavaan", "Mplus")) {
                                GG <- 0
                                indices["rmsea.ci.lower"] <- sqrt(lambda.l/((N -
                                                                                     GG) * df)) * sqrt(G)
                        }
                        else {
                                indices["rmsea.ci.lower"] <- sqrt(lambda.l/(N * df))
                        }
                }
        }

if ("rmsea.ci.upper" %in% fit.measures) {
                upper.lambda <- function(lambda) {
                        (pchisq(X2, df = df, ncp = lambda) - 0.05)
                }
                if (is.na(X2) || is.na(df)) {
                        indices["rmsea.ci.upper"] <- NA
                }
                else if (df < 1 || upper.lambda(N.RMSEA) > 0 || upper.lambda(0) <
                                 0) {
                        indices["rmsea.ci.upper"] <- 0
                }
                else {
                        lambda.u <- try(uniroot(f = upper.lambda, lower = 0,
                                                upper = N.RMSEA)$root, silent = TRUE)
                        if (inherits(lambda.u, "try-error")) {
                                lambda.u <- NA
                        }
                        if (object@Options$mimic %in% c("lavaan", "Mplus")) {
                                GG <- 0
                                indices["rmsea.ci.upper"] <- sqrt(lambda.u/((N -
                                                                                     GG) * df)) * sqrt(G)
                        }
                        else {
                                indices["rmsea.ci.upper"] <- sqrt(lambda.u/(N *
                                                                                    df))
                        }
                }
        }

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: Calculating upper and lower lambda for RMSEA
parts:
The uniroot function is a method to solve an equation numerically. For example, I would like to solve the following equation

(x - 5)^3 + 7 = 0

Then, I will use this code:

FUN <- function(x) (x - 5)^3 + 7

uniroot(f = FUN, lower = 0, upper = 15)$root

In this code, the uniroot function is used to solve for the upper bound and lower bound of the confidence interval of RMSEA. This method is better than the regular confidence interval formula (est +- critvalue*SE) because it does not assume normal sampling distribution.

messages.subject: Re: Calculating upper and lower lambda for RMSEA
parts:
Thanks for the reply.

Now, I understand that the uniroot function in this situation is trying to find lambda for which pchisq equals to 0.95 (if for upper lambda)   

When I tried to compared the ECVI's confidence interval output from Lisrel with output from my home-made function, most of the time, my function produce zero for lower bound of ECVI which is not zero in Lisrel output.

And for the upper bound of ECVI, both outputs are identical.

I suppose it is because of  some conditions like lower.lambda(0) < 0,  upper.lambda(N.RMSEA) > 0 || upper.lambda(0) < 0, but I don't know why.

Could anyone help me to identify what is the problem about the inconsistency of lower bound of ECVs I?

Many thanks.
